newsitem.title: GERMANY: Metro up as 1996 results hit targets.
newsitem.headline: Metro up as 1996 results hit targets.

text.p: German retail giant Metro AG, born out of the merger of three store chains last year, announced group income on ordinary activities of 1.062 billion marks ($627.1 million) for 1996 -- in line with its own and market predictions.

The group's debut net profits came in at 717 million marks, while profits calculated on the DVFA accounting standard were a touch lower at 712 million marks, putting DVFA earnings per share at 7.10 marks.
"The numbers are in line with expectations, and even a touch higher," said Michael Bahlmann, analyst at MM Warburg & Co. The company gave no comparative figures.
Metro stock climbed in early trading on Frankfurt's IBIS electronic market by seven marks to 184.50 marks -- the highest since the merged group first listed last August.
Swiss-controlled Metro, Europe's largest diversified retail group, said it was satisfied with the results after sales came in unchanged at 62 billion marks.
The company, which owns the Kaufhof department store chain and MediaMarkt electronics outlets, said it expected sales to increase by three billion marks this year.
Income on ordinary activities should also rise in 1997, chief executive Michael Wiegandt said in a statement.

"This result expectation is based on our conviction that we will improve results in our business areas, lossmakers will no longer be part of the group and that we still can realise further merger synergies," Wiegandt said.

Metro announced it would propose to the annual general meeting a dividend on ordinary shares of two marks with a two mark bonus, while preferred shares would get a payout of 2.25 marks plus a two mark bonus.

Metro also said it planned to raise its equity capital via a seven-for-five share issue backed by drawing on capital reserves. Through the capital increase, the company's equity would rise from 501 million marks to 1.203 billion marks.
Warburg's Bahlmann said that the two-mark basic dividend implied that Metro might raise its dividend in future.

Looking forward, Wiegandt said he expected West European consumer demand to stagnate for the foreseeable future and even fall in some sectors. At the same time, demand would grow in emerging markets, and especially in eastern Europe, where modern stores would enjoy increasingly bright prospects.
Metro will make internationalising its business a top priority and will seek to optimise its company portfolio to focus on profitability, he said.

Commenting on the performance of individual units, Metro said its electronics shops, department stores and boutiques had all done very well last year. Metro's wholesale business also reinforced its dominant position.
Metro wholesale posted profits of 420 million marks, department stores earned 203 million marks and electronics shops 240 million marks.

Furniture, however, lost 125 million marks after efforts to cut losses failed to meet objectives. Metro said it had sold its Moebel Unger unit effective July 1 to a group of investors and will take a 190 million mark charge on the sale this year.
Profits also fell short of expectations at Metro's building stores (187 million marks), shoe shops (25 million) and computer stores (46 million), the company said.
